claims.text: A Ni-based interlayer between W and CuCrZr mitigates thermal-expansion mismatch under fusion-relevant temperatures.
A Ni-based interlayer increases the mechanical reliability of a W–CuCrZr joint compared with direct W–CuCrZr bonding.
A Ni-based interlayer can be introduced during diffusion bonding or vacuum brazing of W to CuCrZr.
The Ni-based interlayer reduces thermal-expansion-mismatch stress at the W–CuCrZr interfaces.
The Ni-based interlayer improves metallurgical bonding between W and CuCrZr.
Reduced mismatch stress and improved metallurgical bonding lower stress concentrations at the joint.
Reduced mismatch stress and improved metallurgical bonding improve load transfer across the interface.
The Ni-based interlayer enhances the interfacial strength of W–CuCrZr assemblies at elevated temperatures.
The Ni-based interlayer reduces cracking or delamination in W–CuCrZr assemblies at elevated temperatures.
Direct W–CuCrZr bonding without an interlayer is prone to high stress in extreme thermal conditions.
Direct W–CuCrZr bonding without an interlayer is at risk of separation in extreme thermal conditions.
Interlayer performance may depend on the specific thermal cycling conditions.
Performance in actual reactor environments requires further validation.
The magnitudes of the mechanical-property improvement and service-lifetime improvement have not yet been determined experimentally.
